parts.label: (a)
parts.official_mark_scheme_text:
$P(46<X<62)=P\!\left(\frac{46-55}{6}<Z<\frac{62-55}{6}\right)$. [M1]
Guidance: Substitute 46 or 62, mean 55 and standard deviation 6 into a standardisation formula; condone a continuity correction.
$P(46<X<62)=P\!\left(-1.5<Z<\frac76\right)$. [B1]
Guidance: Both standardised endpoint values must be correct, including an unsimplified equivalent.
$P=\Phi\!\left(\frac76\right)-[1-\Phi(1.5)]=0.8784+0.9332-1$. [M1]
Guidance: Calculate the area between the stated normal cumulative probabilities.
$P(46<X<62)=0.812$. [A1]
Guidance: Accept a probability greater than $0.8115$ and at most $0.812$.
Total: 4

parts.label: (b)
parts.official_mark_scheme_text:
$z=-0.674$ (equivalently, the critical magnitude is $0.674$). [B1]
Guidance: The critical normal value must be $-0.674$ (or signed equivalent).
$\frac{36-42}{\sigma}=-0.674$. [M1]
Guidance: Substitute 36 and 42 into the standardisation formula and equate to a normal critical value; do not use a continuity correction or variance in place of standard deviation.
$\sigma=8.90\text{ kg}$. [A1]
Guidance: Award $8.90$ only following the valid standardisation method.
Total: 3

parts.label: (c)
parts.official_mark_scheme_text:
$P(\text{male}<46)=1-0.9332=0.0668$. [M1]
Guidance: Follow through the male probability from part (a), or standardise 46 using mean 55 and standard deviation 6; condone a continuity correction or unsupported correct probability.
$P(\text{female}<46)=\Phi\!\left(\frac{46-42}{8.90}\right)=\Phi(0.449)=0.6732$. [M1]
Guidance: Standardise 46 with female mean 42 and the standard deviation from part (b); follow through that standard deviation and condone a continuity correction.
$P(\text{both})=0.0668\times0.6732$. [M1]
Guidance: Multiply the two probabilities, each strictly between 0 and 1; do not use 0.25 or the final interval probability from part (a).
$P(\text{both})=0.0450$ (or $0.0449$). [A1]
Guidance: Accept values from $0.0449$ to $0.0450$ inclusive.
Total: 4
